stem: Wide World Importers must alert when a custom KQL expression joins two log tables and applies conditional logic that platform metrics cannot express. Which alert type supports this?
explanation: Log search alerts run a Log Analytics KQL query at a set frequency, so they support advanced logic such as joins and conditions that precomputed metrics cannot express. Metric alerts evaluate precomputed metrics and cannot run arbitrary KQL joins. Resource Health alerts report platform-signaled resource health. Smart detection surfaces anomalies automatically and is not a custom-query mechanism.

stem: An operator at Contoso needs a single view that shows every component of a distributed application, the calls between them, and their health, to decide where to start a triage. Which Application Insights experience should they open?
explanation: Application Map gives a visual topology of components and their dependencies with health signals, which is the triage starting point for distributed apps. Live Metrics shows real-time streaming counters, not topology. Transaction search finds individual telemetry items. Usage funnels analyze user behavior, not component health.

stem: After finding a slow operation on the map, a Fabrikam engineer wants a Gantt-style, end-to-end view that correlates server-side telemetry across all monitored components for one operation to find the offending dependency. Which experience provides this?
explanation: The transaction diagnostics, or end-to-end transaction details, view renders a Gantt chart correlating telemetry across components so you can pinpoint the dependency that caused the slowdown. Application Map shows topology but not the per-operation timeline. Metrics explorer charts aggregated metrics. Workbooks are custom reports, not the built-in correlated transaction timeline.

stem: A Tailwind Traders operator wants alerts that notify once when a threshold is breached and again when it clears, with native support for dimensions like instance name and no query to author. Which alert type provides stateful fire-and-resolve with dimensions out of the box?
explanation: Metric alerts are stateful, notifying once on fire and once on resolve, and natively support dimensions without authoring a query. Log search alerts require a KQL query and are more latent. Activity log alerts track discrete events, not threshold state on a metric. Simple log search alerts evaluate rows individually and are stateless per row.

stem: A Northwind vault has purge protection enabled and a secret was soft-deleted yesterday. An operator with subscription Owner rights tries to purge it immediately to reuse the name. What happens?
choices: The purge succeeds because Owner overrides purge protection
The purge is blocked; the object cannot be purged until the retention period elapses
The purge succeeds only if the operator also holds Key Vault Purge Operator
Purge protection is automatically disabled after 24 hours
explanation: With purge protection enabled, a soft-deleted object cannot be purged by anyone, including Owners and Microsoft, until the mandatory retention period elapses. No role, including Owner or Purge Operator, can override purge protection. Purge protection cannot be disabled once enabled, so it does not lapse after a day.

stem: During a review, a Woodgrove Bank engineer proposes turning off purge protection on a production vault to speed up name reuse after deletions. What is the correct constraint to cite?
choices: Once purge protection is enabled it cannot be disabled or overridden by anyone, including Microsoft
Purge protection can be disabled only within the first 7 days
Purge protection can be toggled off by a Key Vault Administrator at any time
Disabling purge protection requires the access policy model
explanation: Purge protection, once enabled, cannot be disabled or circumvented by any role or by Microsoft; the vault name cannot be reused until deletion recovery or retention expiry. No administrator role can disable it. There is no 7-day grace window to turn it off. The permission model does not provide a way to disable purge protection.

stem: Relecloud rotates a secret in Key Vault automatically every 30 days. Their app loads it through an App Configuration Key Vault reference and must pick up new secret versions without changing the sentinel key or redeploying. Which App Configuration setting accomplishes this?
choices: Disable soft delete on the vault so new versions replace old ones
Reference a specific secret version in the Key Vault reference
Lower the configuration refresh interval to one second
Set a Key Vault secret refresh interval independent of the configuration refresh cycle
explanation: App Configuration lets you configure a Key Vault secret refresh interval independent of the config refresh, so the provider periodically reloads rotated secrets even though the reference URI is unchanged. Referencing a specific version pins the value so rotation is never picked up. Lowering the config refresh interval does not reload Key Vault secrets whose reference did not change. Soft delete is unrelated to reloading versions.

stem: A Proseware architect debates whether the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro or Kusto queries should be described as the tool that collects telemetry versus the tool that analyzes it. Which pairing is correct?
choices: Both instrument the app; neither analyzes
The Distro instruments and exports telemetry; KQL in Log Analytics analyzes the stored telemetry
Both analyze; instrumentation is done by metric alerts
The Distro analyzes telemetry; KQL in Log Analytics instruments the app
explanation: The Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro instruments the application and exports traces, metrics, and logs; KQL queries analyze that data after it is stored in Log Analytics. The roles are not reversed; KQL does not instrument. The Distro does not analyze, and metric alerts do not instrument code.

stem: A Litware finance team must forecast alert cost. They will run one KQL query every 5 minutes as a log search alert and separately monitor a platform metric across 200 resource instances with one metric alert rule. Which cost driver pairing is correct?
choices: Log search alert is billed per query evaluation interval; metric alert is billed per monitored time series
Both are billed as a flat monthly fee regardless of scope
Log search alert is billed per evaluated time series; metric alert is billed per query evaluation
Both are billed per gigabyte of ingested logs
explanation: Log search alert rules are billed based on how often the query is evaluated (more frequent evaluation costs more), while metric alert rules are billed based on the number of time series monitored. The two drivers are reversed in the first option. Neither alert type is billed purely by log ingestion volume, nor as a flat fee independent of frequency or time series.

stem: A Fourth Coffee low-traffic Node.js function app rarely hits its telemetry quota. The team wants sampling that does not reduce traffic until a minimum rate is reached, so low-use periods keep full telemetry. Which sampling type matches, noting its platform support?
choices: Adaptive sampling, which is the default for ASP.NET, ASP.NET Core, and Azure Functions server-side telemetry
Browser sampling, which only applies to page views
Fixed-rate sampling, which discards a constant percentage regardless of load
Ingestion sampling, which runs at the service endpoint for all sources
explanation: Adaptive sampling adjusts volume based on load and does not reduce traffic below a minimum rate, so low-use apps are effectively not sampled; it is the default for ASP.NET/ASP.NET Core and Azure Functions. Ingestion sampling drops a set percentage at the endpoint regardless of load. Fixed-rate sampling always discards a constant percentage, sampling even low-traffic periods. Browser sampling is not a low-load-aware server option.

stem: An Adventure Works Python service should authenticate to Key Vault with no secrets in code, using the local developer sign-in during development and a managed identity in production without code changes. Which credential type meets this?
choices: An account key stored in appsettings.json
ManagedIdentityCredential hardcoded to a client ID for all environments
A client secret loaded from an environment variable
explanation: DefaultAzureCredential tries multiple methods at runtime, using the developer sign-in locally and a managed identity in Azure, so the same code works across environments without stored secrets. A client secret reintroduces a stored credential. Hardcoding ManagedIdentityCredential to a client ID does not work for local development. An account key in config is a stored secret and is not how Key Vault authenticates.

stem: A Coho Vineyard workload runs on an on-premises Kubernetes cluster outside Azure and must reach Microsoft Entra protected resources without storing certificates that expire. Which approach removes the expiring credential?
choices: Assign a system-assigned managed identity to the cluster node pool
Store a rotating certificate in Key Vault and mount it into the pod
Use workload identity federation so the cluster token is exchanged for a Microsoft Entra token
Embed an app registration client secret as a Kubernetes secret
explanation: Workload identity federation lets the external Kubernetes token be exchanged for a Microsoft Entra access token via a federated credential on a user-assigned identity or app registration, eliminating stored certificates or secrets. Mounting a certificate or embedding a client secret still manages an expiring credential. A system-assigned managed identity is not available to workloads running outside Azure and does not support federated credentials.

stem:
Complete the KQL so it reports the 95th percentile request duration per one-hour bucket. Which token fills the blank?

```
requests
| where timestamp > ago(24h)
| summarize percentile(duration, 95) by ________(timestamp, 1h)
```
explanation: bin() reduces a numeric or datetime column to discrete buckets, so bin(timestamp, 1h) groups rows into one-hour intervals for the per-bucket percentile. floor rounds a number but does not create datetime buckets for grouping. range generates a series, it is not a grouping function inside summarize. truncate is not the KQL bucketing operator here.

stem:
Complete the KQL join so every request row is kept even when it has no matching dependency row, to find requests with zero downstream calls. Which join kind fills the blank?

```
requests
| join kind=________ (
    dependencies
    | project operation_Id, target
) on operation_Id
```
explanation: leftouter returns all rows from the left (requests) plus matching right rows, leaving unmatched right columns null, so requests with no dependency are kept. inner drops requests without a match. rightsemi returns only right-table rows that match. leftanti returns only left rows with no match, discarding the ones that do have dependencies.

stem:
Complete the KQL that validates whether sampling is active by computing the retained percentage per telemetry type. Which expression fills the blank?

```
union requests, dependencies, exceptions, traces
| where timestamp > ago(1d)
| summarize RetainedPercentage = ________ by bin(timestamp, 1h), itemType
```
explanation: Each retained record carries an itemCount equal to the number of items it represents, so 100/avg(itemCount) yields the retained percentage; values below 100 indicate sampling. avg(itemCount)*100 inflates the value rather than inverting it. count()/100 counts rows, not a percentage. sum(itemCount) gives the true item total, not a retained percentage.

stem:
Complete the KQL so it returns the true request count per bin under sampling, then orders newest first. Which pair of tokens fills the blanks in order?

```
requests
| where timestamp > ago(6h)
| summarize TrueCount = ________ by bin(timestamp, 30m)
| ________ by timestamp desc
```
explanation: sum(itemCount) reconstructs the sampling-corrected total, and order by timestamp desc sorts newest first (order and sort are synonyms in KQL). count() undercounts under sampling. dcount with sort asc gives distinct counts ordered oldest first. avg(itemCount) with top does not produce a full ordered total count.

stem:
Complete the Python Azure App Configuration load call so the provider triggers a full refresh only when a sentinel key named AppSentinel changes. Which argument fills the blank?

```
config = load(
    endpoint,
    credential,
    ________=[WatchedKey(key="AppSentinel")]
)
```
explanation: The Python provider uses refresh_on with a WatchedKey to monitor the sentinel key and refresh the whole configuration when it changes. selectors chooses which keys to load, not which to watch. key_vault_options configures Key Vault reference resolution. feature_flag_enabled toggles feature flags, not refresh watching.

RegisterAll monitors all loaded keys so any change triggers a full refresh, which is the no-sentinel approach in the .NET provider. Register(key) monitors a single key such as a sentinel, not all keys. SetDirty forces a refresh check but does not register monitoring. EnableFeatureFlags is unrelated to key refresh registration.

stem: A Contoso security baseline must both make deleted Key Vault objects recoverable AND enforce a retention that no administrator can override during the window. Which two Key Vault settings, together, achieve this? (Select two.)
choices: Switch to the access policy permission model
Assign the Key Vault Reader role broadly
explanation: Soft delete provides recoverability of deleted objects, and purge protection enforces a mandatory retention that cannot be overridden, so both together satisfy the baseline. The access policy model is a legacy authorization choice, not a deletion protection. Key Vault Reader controls read access, not deletion recovery. Disabling public network access is a network control unrelated to purge and recovery behavior.

stem: Fabrikam wants to configure workload identity federation. On which two Microsoft Entra identity objects can a federated identity credential be configured? (Select two.)
explanation: Federated identity credentials can be configured on a user-assigned managed identity or on an app registration to trust an external identity provider. System-assigned managed identities do not support federated identity credentials. An RBAC role definition and a Key Vault access policy are authorization constructs, not identities that hold federated credentials.

stem: An Adventure Works team evaluates ingestion sampling in Application Insights. Which two statements about ingestion sampling are correct? (Select two.)
choices: It runs at the Application Insights service endpoint
It is ignored when SDK adaptive or fixed-rate sampling is already in effect
It reduces the telemetry traffic sent from the application
It requires redeploying the app to change the rate
It only applies to custom metrics
explanation: Ingestion sampling operates at the service endpoint and is disabled when the SDK is already sampling a telemetry type. It does not reduce traffic sent from the app; it drops data after arrival. Its rate is set in the portal without redeploying. It is not limited to custom metrics, and preaggregated metrics are always kept regardless.

stem: Under Azure RBAC for Key Vault, which two built-in roles carry the right to grant others data-plane access, making them the roles to tightly control? (Select two.)
choices: Key Vault Crypto Service Encryption User
explanation: Azure RBAC restricts the ability to grant access to the Owner and User Access Administrator roles, which is a security advantage over access policies. Key Vault Secrets User only reads secret values. Key Vault Reader reads metadata. Crypto Service Encryption User is a scoped crypto role. None of those three can grant access to others.

stem: A Litware app has adaptive sampling enabled. Which two telemetry categories are always retained and remain accurate regardless of the sampling rate? (Select two.)
explanation: Performance metrics and custom preaggregated metrics are always kept regardless of sampling, which is why metrics stay accurate even when log-based counts are affected. Dependency, request, and trace telemetry are event telemetry subject to sampling, so their retained rows must be corrected with sum(itemCount) for accurate counts.

stem: Northwind Traders wants a new Azure Key Vault where deleted secrets stay recoverable for exactly 30 days, and they want that window to be immutable once the vault is running. Which statement about configuring this is correct?
choices: The retention period must be set to 30 days at vault creation and cannot be changed afterward
The soft-delete retention period can be lowered from 90 to 30 days at any time after creation
Retention is fixed at 90 days and cannot be customized
Retention is configured on each secret individually rather than on the vault
explanation: The soft-delete retention interval is configurable from 7 to 90 days but can only be set when the vault is created; once set and saved it cannot be changed for that vault, which matches the immutable 30-day requirement. You cannot lower the interval after creation, so the first option is wrong. Retention is customizable, not fixed at 90, so the third is wrong. Retention is a vault-level property, not per-secret, so the fourth is wrong.

stem: Woodgrove Bank enabled purge protection on a production key vault to satisfy an insider-threat control. A subscription owner now files a ticket asking to turn purge protection off for one vault. What is the correct response?
choices: An owner can disable purge protection through Azure Resource Manager
Once enabled, purge protection cannot be disabled or overridden by anyone, including Microsoft
Purge protection can be disabled only by Microsoft support
Purge protection is disabled automatically when the vault is switched to the RBAC model
explanation: Purge protection is designed so that no administrator role or permission can override it; once enabled it cannot be disabled or overridden by anyone, including Microsoft, until the resource is deleted. No owner role can turn it off, so option one is wrong. Microsoft explicitly cannot override it, so option two is wrong. The permission model is unrelated to purge protection, so option four is wrong.

stem: Litware, Inc. runs one shared key vault. Application A must read only the single secret named db-conn, while other apps must not gain access to it. The team uses the RBAC permission model. What is the least-privilege way to grant this?
choices: Assign Key Vault Secrets User at the vault scope
Add an access policy granting Get on all secrets
Assign Key Vault Secrets User scoped to the individual secret db-conn
Assign Key Vault Administrator scoped to the resource group
explanation: Azure RBAC for Key Vault supports assigning a role at the individual key, secret, or certificate scope, so Key Vault Secrets User scoped to db-conn grants read of only that one secret. Vault-scope Secrets User exposes every secret. Access policies apply only at vault scope and cannot target one secret. Key Vault Administrator is far broader than a single-secret read.

stem: A Fabrikam microservice running on Azure needs to read secret values from a vault that uses Azure RBAC, but it must never be able to create, update, or delete secrets. Which built-in role fits?
explanation: Key Vault Secrets User grants read of secret contents only, which is the minimum needed to fetch values without any write or delete rights. Secrets Officer can perform any action on secrets including set and delete. Administrator grants full data-plane control. Reader sees metadata only and cannot read secret values.

stem: Contoso Energy delegates key lifecycle work to a platform team. The team must configure key rotation policies and rotate keys on demand in an RBAC-enabled vault, but must not read or export secret values. Which role assignment is correct?
explanation: The Key Vault key rotation feature requires key management permissions; Microsoft documents assigning Key Vault Crypto Officer to manage the rotation policy and perform on-demand rotation. Secrets Officer governs secrets, not keys. Crypto User can perform cryptographic operations but cannot manage rotation policy. Administrator is broader than least privilege and also covers secrets.

stem: Adventure Works must store cryptographic keys where the customer solely controls the root of trust, the instance is dedicated to only their tenant, and the keys are protected by FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated hardware. Which option meets all three requirements?
choices: Azure App Configuration with customer-managed keys
explanation: Managed HSM is single-tenant, uses FIPS 140-3 Level 3 validated HSMs, and gives the customer a customer-controlled security domain, so it is the only option meeting all three constraints. Standard is multitenant and FIPS 140-2 Level 1 software-backed. Premium is FIPS 140-3 Level 3 but multitenant with a Microsoft-controlled root of trust. App Configuration stores configuration, not HSM-backed keys.

stem: Tailwind Traders uses a customer-managed key in Azure Key Vault to encrypt a storage account, and enables automatic key rotation. They must ensure the storage service picks up each new key version without manual reconfiguration. How should the key be referenced?
choices: By a versioned key identifier that includes the specific key version
By the key vault resource ID rather than a key URI
By a versionless key identifier that omits the version
By a secret reference instead of a key reference
explanation: A versionless key URI lets the service automatically move to the latest key version after rotation, enabling zero-touch customer-managed key rotation. A versioned URI pins one version and will not follow rotation. A resource ID does not identify a specific key for cryptographic use. A key is not a secret, so a secret reference is inappropriate.

stem: Relecloud enabled the Key Vault firewall with the option to allow trusted Microsoft services to bypass it. A security reviewer asks whether a bypassing trusted service can therefore read any secret. What is accurate?
choices: Trusted-service bypass grants data access without any authentication
The bypass automatically assigns the service the Key Vault Secrets User role
The bypass applies to control-plane operations only
A bypassing service still must present a valid Microsoft Entra token and hold permissions for the operation
explanation: The firewall bypass only lets the network request reach the vault; the service still must present a valid Microsoft Entra token and have RBAC or access-policy permissions to perform the operation. Bypass never removes authentication. It grants no roles automatically. Firewall rules govern the data plane, not the control plane, so the last option is wrong.

stem: Proseware updates several related keys in Azure App Configuration and wants dependent applications to reload the whole set only once, after all edits are complete, to avoid reading a half-updated configuration. Which approach achieves this?
choices: Monitor a single sentinel key and update it last, after all other keys change
Register every key individually so each change triggers a refresh
Disable the refresh interval so changes apply instantly
Store all keys under one label and refresh on label change
explanation: A sentinel key is monitored instead of every key; by updating it only after all other changes are complete, the app reloads the full configuration exactly once, preserving consistency. Registering every key can trigger multiple partial reloads. Disabling the interval does not coordinate a single consistent reload. Labels select variants but do not provide the update-last consistency signal.

stem: Alpine Ski House stores a database password in Key Vault and references it from Azure App Configuration. The password is rotated in Key Vault every 12 hours, but the App Configuration key-value that references it never changes. How should the app pick up the rotated secret?
choices: Shorten the App Configuration configuration refresh interval only
Configure an independent Key Vault secret refresh interval on the provider
Recreate the Key Vault reference each time the secret rotates
Switch the reference to store the secret value directly in App Configuration
explanation: App Configuration lets you set a secret refresh interval independent of the configuration refresh cycle; because the reference URI is unchanged while the underlying secret rotates, only a secret refresh interval forces the provider to re-fetch the current value. A shorter configuration refresh does not help because the reference key-value never changes. Recreating the reference is unnecessary manual work. Storing the value directly defeats the purpose of keeping the secret in Key Vault.

stem: Margie's Travel attaches a system-assigned managed identity to a virtual machine and grants it Key Vault access. Later the VM is deleted. What happens to the identity and its role assignments?
choices: The identity persists and can be reattached to another resource
The identity remains but its role assignments are transferred to the resource group
The identity is deleted automatically along with the VM
The identity converts to a user-assigned managed identity
explanation: A system-assigned managed identity is tied to the lifecycle of its resource; when the resource is deleted, Azure automatically deletes the identity and its role assignments. A system-assigned identity cannot be reattached elsewhere; only user-assigned identities are standalone. Role assignments are not transferred. The identity type does not convert on deletion.

stem: Lamna Healthcare wants a GitHub Actions workflow to authenticate to Azure and read Key Vault secrets using workload identity federation, with no stored client secret. Which identity target can a federated identity credential be configured on?
choices: A Key Vault access policy principal
A user-assigned managed identity or an app registration
explanation: Workload identity federation is configured only on a user-assigned managed identity or an app registration; the federated identity credential defines which external token is trusted. System-assigned managed identities do not support federated identity credentials. An access-policy principal and a security group are not valid targets for a federated identity credential.

stem: A Trey Research application uses DefaultAzureCredential from the Azure Identity library. The developers want to know which credential is attempted first in the default chain. Which is it?
explanation: In the DefaultAzureCredential chain, EnvironmentCredential is attempted first, reading environment variables for a configured service principal. Workload Identity is second and Managed Identity third. Azure CLI is a later developer-tool credential in the chain, not first.

stem: Fourth Coffee has a key vault configured with legacy access policies and plans to switch it to the Azure RBAC permission model. What must the team account for during the change?
choices: Access policies and RBAC apply simultaneously with no impact
Setting the RBAC permission model invalidates all existing access policy permissions, which can cause outages if equivalent roles are not assigned
RBAC can only be enabled on a brand-new vault, never an existing one
Switching to RBAC also disables soft delete
explanation: Setting the Azure RBAC permission model invalidates all access-policy permissions, so equivalent Azure roles must be assigned first to avoid an access outage. The two models do not run together on one vault. RBAC can be enabled on existing vaults. Soft delete is independent of the permission model.

stem: An auditor at Humongous Insurance needs to view the names, properties, and expiration dates of keys and secrets in an RBAC-enabled vault, but must never see any secret value or key material. Which role satisfies least privilege?
explanation: Key Vault Reader reads metadata of the vault and its keys, secrets, and certificates but cannot read sensitive values such as secret contents or key material. Secrets User can read secret contents. Administrator has full data access. Crypto User can perform key operations, exceeding read-only metadata needs.

stem: Coho Vineyard grants an engineer the subscription Owner role, expecting that this alone will let the engineer perform key operations on a Managed HSM. What is the actual behavior?
choices: Owner at the subscription automatically grants Managed HSM data-plane key access
Owner grants read but not write access to Managed HSM keys
The engineer receives the Key Vault Administrator role on the Managed HSM
Management-plane access to a Managed HSM does not grant any data-plane access to keys; local RBAC must be assigned separately
explanation: Unlike key vaults, granting management-plane access to a Managed HSM does not grant any data-plane access; Managed HSM local RBAC role assignments are required and enforced by the HSM itself. Owner grants no data-plane access, so options one and three are wrong. Managed HSM uses its own local roles, not the vault Key Vault Administrator role.

stem: VanArsdel needs a named, immutable point-in-time set of App Configuration key-values that is guaranteed not to change after creation, so a deployment can pin exactly the configuration it was tested against. Which feature provides this?
explanation: A snapshot is a named, immutable subset of a store's key-values chosen by key and label filters at creation; once created its contents are guaranteed to remain unchanged. A sentinel key is a refresh trigger, not immutable content. A Key Vault reference points to an external secret. A label groups variants but is not immutable.

stem: First Up Consultants enables geo-replication on an Azure App Configuration store and uses the provider library. How does the client behave during a regional problem with the primary replica?
choices: The application must be manually reconfigured to point at a replica
The provider automatically discovers replicas and fails over to a healthy one
Geo-replication only copies data for backup and cannot serve reads
The application must restart to pick up a replica
explanation: The App Configuration provider library automatically discovers the store's replicas and uses them if an issue arises, providing failover without manual intervention or a restart. No manual reconfiguration is needed. Replicas serve live reads, not just backup. No restart is required for failover.

stem: Best For You Organics configured a federated identity credential for a GitHub workflow, but token exchange fails without any error message. The most likely cause relates to which requirement?
choices: The audience value must be a random GUID
The subject supports wildcard matching by default
The issuer, subject, and audience must case-sensitively match the claims in the incoming external token
The federated credential name must equal the subject
explanation: The federated identity credential issuer, subject, and audience must case-sensitively match the corresponding claims in the external token; a mismatch causes the exchange to fail, often silently. The recommended audience is api://AzureADTokenExchange, not a GUID. Wildcards are not supported in standard federated identity credentials. The name is an independent identifier, unrelated to the subject.

stem: Litware Foods keeps one key named AppConnection in Azure App Configuration but needs distinct values for the dev, test, and prod environments under that same key name. Which App Configuration feature stores these distinct values?
explanation: Labels let a single key hold multiple values distinguished by label, so the same key name can carry dev, test, and prod values selected by a label filter. Sentinel keys trigger refresh, snapshots are immutable subsets, and Key Vault references point to external secrets; none of these differentiate values of one key by environment.

stem: Munson's Pickles rotates a customer-managed key that wraps data encryption keys for an Azure service. To avoid disrupting decryption of already-encrypted data immediately after rotation, what must the team do with the previous key version?
choices: Keep both the old and new key versions enabled until re-wrapping is complete
Delete the previous key version right after rotation
Export the previous version and store it outside Key Vault
Disable soft delete so old versions are purged quickly
explanation: Rotation re-wraps data encryption keys with the new key version rather than re-encrypting the underlying data, so existing data still depends on the old version; both versions must remain enabled until re-wrapping completes. Deleting or disabling the old version too early breaks decryption of existing data. Exporting it is unnecessary and insecure. Purging via disabling soft delete does not help and reduces recoverability.

stem: The Phone Company adds a Key Vault reference to Azure App Configuration. A developer asks what App Configuration actually stores for that key-value and how the provider resolves it. Which description is correct?
choices: App Configuration stores the plaintext secret value copied from Key Vault
App Configuration stores a reference marked by a special content type, and the provider retrieves the actual secret from Key Vault at load time
App Configuration stores an encrypted copy of the secret that only the provider can decrypt
App Configuration stores the Key Vault access key so clients can authenticate
explanation: A Key Vault reference stores a pointer to the secret, identified by a unique content type; the configuration provider recognizes it and connects to Key Vault to retrieve the actual value at load time. App Configuration never copies the plaintext or an encrypted copy of the secret. It does not store Key Vault credentials; the client authenticates with its own identity.

stem: Consolidated Messenger enables automatic key rotation on several keys in a Managed HSM with a short creation-based interval. Over time an operator worries about hitting a service limit. Which Managed HSM constraint applies to rotation?
choices: Managed HSM allows unlimited key versions per key
Managed HSM caps automatic rotation at one version per year
Managed HSM has a limit of 100 versions per key, and rotation-created versions count toward it
Managed HSM does not support automatic key rotation
explanation: Managed HSM has a limit of 100 versions per key, and key versions created by automatic or manual rotation count toward that limit. Versions are not unlimited. Rotation frequency is not capped at once per year, though the automatic minimum is 28 days. Managed HSM does support automatic rotation.

stem: School of Fine Art wants a governance principal that can grant and revoke Key Vault data-plane roles such as Key Vault Secrets User for other principals, but should not itself be able to read secret values. Which role best fits?
explanation: Key Vault Data Access Administrator manages access by adding or removing the Key Vault data-plane role assignments, with an ABAC condition constraining which roles, without granting the ability to read secret values. Key Vault Administrator grants full data access including reading secrets. Owner can assign any role and is far broader. Secrets Officer manages secret data, not role assignments.

stem: Graphic Design Institute disables public network access on a key vault and uses a private endpoint. A monitoring tool reports that the vault's public DNS name still resolves to an IP address. How should this be interpreted?
choices: Public DNS records remaining resolvable is by design; disabling public access blocks data-plane connections, not DNS resolution
The private endpoint failed and public access is still open
Soft delete must be turned off to hide the DNS record
The vault must be recreated to remove the public record
explanation: Disabling public access blocks public data-plane connections, but the vault's public DNS records remain resolvable by design; resolution does not mean the data plane is reachable. DNS resolving does not indicate a failed endpoint or open access. Soft delete is unrelated to DNS. Recreating the vault does not change this designed behavior.

stem: Wide World Importers automates many external pipelines and tries to add a large number of federated identity credentials to a single user-assigned managed identity. They hit a ceiling. What is the standard maximum number of federated identity credentials per application or user-assigned managed identity?
explanation: A maximum of 20 federated identity credentials can be added to a single application or user-assigned managed identity. The documented limit is 20, so 5 and 10 are too low and 100 is too high; the 100-version figure belongs to Managed HSM key versions, not federated credentials.

stem: Contoso Pharmaceuticals needs an identity that can create and manage certificates in an RBAC-enabled vault, including certificate policies, but must not manage keys or secrets. Which built-in role is the least-privilege fit?
explanation: Key Vault Certificates Officer performs any action on certificates in the vault except manage permissions, scoping the grant to certificates only. Administrator covers keys, secrets, and certificates. Crypto Officer manages keys. Secrets Officer manages secrets. Only Certificates Officer is limited to certificates.

stem:
Northwind Traders enables purge protection on an existing vault so soft-deleted objects cannot be purged before the retention window elapses. Complete the Azure CLI flag.

```
az keyvault update \
  --name nw-prod-kv \
  --resource-group nw-rg \
  --enable-________ true
```
explanation: The --enable-purge-protection flag turns on purge protection, enforcing the mandatory retention period against purging. --enable-soft-delete governs recoverability, not the no-purge enforcement. --enable-rbac-authorization sets the permission model. --public-network-access controls networking, not deletion protection.

stem:
Fabrikam provisions a new key vault that must use Azure RBAC rather than legacy access policies for data-plane authorization. Complete the Azure CLI flag.

```
az keyvault create \
  --name fab-kv \
  --resource-group fab-rg \
  --location eastus \
  --enable-________ true
```
explanation: --enable-rbac-authorization sets the vault to the Azure RBAC permission model for data-plane operations. --enable-purge-protection and --enable-soft-delete are recovery features, not the authorization model. There is no --enable-managed-hsm flag on az keyvault create.

stem:
Woodgrove Bank creates a federated identity credential on a user-assigned managed identity so GitHub Actions can exchange its token. Complete the parameter that specifies the accepted token audience.

```
az identity federated-credential create \
  --name gh-deploy \
  --identity-name wg-uami \
  --resource-group wg-rg \
  --issuer "https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com" \
  --subject "repo:woodgrove/deploy:ref:refs/heads/main" \
  --________ "api://AzureADTokenExchange"
```
explanation: The --audiences parameter sets the accepted aud claim value; api://AzureADTokenExchange is the recommended value for Microsoft Entra token exchange. --issuer and --subject are already supplied and identify the provider and workload. --name is the credential identifier, not the audience.

stem:
Relecloud loads Azure App Configuration in Python and must force Key Vault-referenced secrets to be re-fetched every two hours, independent of the configuration refresh cycle, so rotated secrets are picked up. Complete the load parameter.

```
from azure.appconfiguration.provider import load
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential

config = load(
    endpoint=endpoint,
    credential=DefaultAzureCredential(),
    keyvault_credential=DefaultAzureCredential(),
    ________=7200
)
```
explanation: secret_refresh_interval sets an independent interval that forces the provider to retrieve fresh Key Vault secret values, decoupled from the configuration refresh cycle. refresh_interval governs configuration key refresh, not secrets. startup_timeout controls initial load time. replica_discovery_enabled toggles geo-replica discovery.

RegisterAll instructs the provider to reload the entire configuration whenever any selected key-value changes, without needing a sentinel key. Register monitors a single specified key. SetRefreshInterval sets timing, not what to watch. SelectSnapshot loads a snapshot and is not a refresh registration call.

stem: Fabrikam must choose Azure Key Vault Managed HSM specifically because two properties distinguish it from the Premium vault tier. Which two properties are unique to Managed HSM? (Select two.)
choices: It is a single-tenant service dedicated to one customer
The customer controls the root of trust through a customer-owned security domain
It is multitenant and operated on shared HSMs
Keys are software-protected rather than HSM-backed
It is validated only to FIPS 140-2 Level 1
explanation: Managed HSM is single-tenant and gives the customer control of the root of trust via a customer-owned security domain; both distinguish it from the multitenant, Microsoft-root-of-trust Premium tier. Multitenant shared HSMs describe Premium and Standard, not Managed HSM. Software-protected keys and FIPS 140-2 Level 1 describe the Standard tier.

stem: A Litware pipeline configures a federated identity credential. Beyond the audience value, which two settings must case-sensitively match the claims in the incoming external token for the exchange to be authorized? (Select two.)
explanation: The issuer and subject of the federated identity credential must case-sensitively match the issuer and subject claims in the external token, in addition to the audience. name is a local identifier for the credential, description is free text, and the creation timestamp is metadata; none of these are matched against token claims.

stem: A Proseware service running on Azure must read secret values from an RBAC-enabled vault and also list the metadata of keys, without any write or delete rights. Which two built-in roles together provide exactly this least-privilege access? (Select two.)
explanation: Key Vault Secrets User grants read of secret contents, and Key Vault Reader grants read of key, secret, and certificate metadata; together they satisfy read-only value plus metadata needs. Secrets Officer and Administrator both add write and delete rights beyond least privilege. Crypto Officer manages key rotation and policy, exceeding read-only metadata.

stem: Tailwind Traders wants an App Configuration deployment that both guarantees a consistent, unchanging set of values for one release AND stays available if the primary region has an outage. Which two features together address these two goals? (Select two.)
explanation: Snapshots provide an immutable, consistent set of key-values for a release, and geo-replication with automatic provider failover keeps configuration available during a regional outage. A sentinel key coordinates refresh timing, labels select value variants, and a Key Vault reference externalizes secrets; none of these provide immutability plus regional availability together.

stem: With AZURE_TOKEN_CREDENTIALS set to prod, a Woodgrove app relies on DefaultAzureCredential in a deployed Azure host. Which two of the following are deployed-service credentials attempted in that chain, rather than developer-tool credentials? (Select two.)
explanation: Workload Identity and Managed Identity are deployed-service credentials in the DefaultAzureCredential chain, used when the app runs on an Azure host. Azure CLI, Azure PowerShell, and Visual Studio Code are developer-tool credentials excluded when the chain is restricted to production deployed-service credentials.

stem: A Contoso ASP.NET Core service sets the Application Insights connection string in three places at once: a value passed to UseAzureMonitor in code, an APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING environment variable, and an appsettings.json AzureMonitor section. Which source does the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro actually use?
choices: The Distro fails to start because of the conflict
The value set in code via UseAzureMonitor
explanation: For the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro the connection string precedence is code, then environment variable, then configuration file, so the value set in code via UseAzureMonitor wins. The environment variable and appsettings.json values are both overridden by the code value. The Distro does not error on multiple sources; it deterministically applies the documented precedence.

stem: A Fabrikam Python service running the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro sets OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES to include service.name=orders-legacy and also sets OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=orders-api. Which value becomes the service.name resource attribute used as the Cloud Role Name?
choices: orders-legacy, because OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES is more specific
Both values are concatenated into one role name
explanation: When service.name is provided in both OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME takes precedence and sets the service.name resource attribute. OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES does not override OTEL_SERVICE_NAME for service.name. The two values are not concatenated, and the attribute is not cleared.

stem: Woodgrove Bank runs a Java application with the Application Insights agent. The connection string is present as a -Dapplicationinsights.connection.string system property, as the APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING environment variable, and inside applicationinsights.json. Which source does the agent use?
choices: The agent rejects all three and sends nothing
explanation: For the Java agent the precedence is system property, then environment variable, then configuration file, so the -D system property wins. The environment variable and JSON file are both lower precedence than the system property. The agent does not reject the configuration when multiple sources are set.

stem: Adventure Works extends distributed tracing so a downstream service continues the same operation, and a developer inspects the W3C traceparent header on the outgoing request. Which segment of traceparent becomes the Application Insights Operation_Id that groups every span of the trace?
explanation: The W3C trace-id maps to Application Insights Operation_Id, so all telemetry sharing that trace-id is grouped into one end-to-end operation. The parent-id (span-id) maps to the individual Id and Operation_ParentId, not the operation grouping key. Trace-flags carry the sampling decision, and version identifies the header format, neither of which correlate spans.

stem: In a Relecloud trace, a dependency row and the downstream request row it triggered must be linked as parent and child so the transaction tree renders correctly. Which Application Insights field on the child request holds the id of the calling dependency span?
explanation: Operation_ParentId holds the parent span's id (the W3C parent-id of the parent span), which links a child request to the dependency that called it. Operation_Id is the shared trace-id for the whole operation, not the parent link. Id is the child's own span id. Operation_Name is the logical name, not a correlation pointer.

stem: A Proseware browser app and its server share one Application Insights resource. The team needs W3C traceparent headers emitted on outgoing AJAX calls while keeping compatibility with an older service that still reads the legacy Request-Id format. Which distributedTracingMode value meets both needs?
explanation: AI_AND_W3C emits W3C trace context (traceparent and tracestate) plus the legacy AI Request-Id headers, preserving back-compatibility with services instrumented only for the older format. W3C emits only the new headers and can break the legacy service. AI emits only the legacy format and omits traceparent. Disabled turns correlation off entirely.

stem: A Fourth Coffee ASP.NET Core app uses the classic Application Insights SDK with no sampling configuration added. During a traffic spike telemetry volume is automatically reduced. Which sampling type is in effect by default, and at roughly what target?
choices: Adaptive sampling at about five telemetry items per second
No sampling until it is explicitly enabled
explanation: Adaptive sampling is enabled by default in the ASP.NET and ASP.NET Core SDKs, targeting about five telemetry items per second and adjusting to the observed volume. Fixed-rate and ingestion sampling are not the defaults and must be configured. Sampling is not off by default in these SDKs.

stem: Litware wants to reduce telemetry from both browser and server while still being able to navigate from a page view to its related server request in Transaction Search. Which sampling type is designed to keep those related client and server items together?
explanation: Fixed-rate sampling synchronizes the client and server sampling decisions so related items, such as a page view and its request, are retained together for navigation in Search. Adaptive sampling is server-side only and does not synchronize with the browser. Ingestion sampling happens at the endpoint and does not coordinate client and server SDK decisions. No sampling would not reduce volume.

stem: Tailwind Traders sets an ingestion sampling rate of 50 percent in the portal, but their ASP.NET Core app already has adaptive sampling active. Support reports the ingestion rate appears to be ignored. Why?
choices: Ingestion sampling applies only when no SDK-side sampling is in effect
Ingestion sampling requires the Premium tier
The portal value must match the SDK value exactly
Ingestion sampling only samples browser telemetry
explanation: When the service endpoint detects SDK sampling already active (a rate below 100 percent), it ignores the configured ingestion sampling rate; ingestion sampling applies only when no other sampling is in operation. There is no tier requirement for ingestion sampling. The portal and SDK values do not need to match. Ingestion sampling is not limited to browser telemetry.

stem: After enabling aggressive sampling, a Northwind team worries their request-rate dashboards are now inaccurate, yet the standard request-count metric in the Metrics pane still reports correct totals. Which mechanism explains the accurate metric despite sampling?
choices: Log-based queries automatically multiply by itemCount
Preaggregated (standard) metrics are computed before sampling and are not affected by it
The metric is estimated from a moving average
explanation: SDKs compute preaggregated standard metrics before sampling discards items, so those metrics stay accurate even when log-based queries are affected by high sample rates. Log-based queries need manual sum(itemCount) correction and are not automatically exact. Sampling can apply to requests. The metric is a true preaggregate, not a moving-average estimate.

stem: Wingtip Toys relies on custom metrics and performance counters for alerting and wants certainty that sampling will never drop them. Which statement is correct about these telemetry types?
choices: Custom and performance metrics are always kept and are not subject to sampling
They are sampled at the same rate as requests
They are kept only if OperationId is set
They are kept only under fixed-rate sampling
explanation: Some telemetry types, including performance metrics and custom metrics, are always kept regardless of whether sampling is enabled. They are not sampled alongside requests. Retention does not depend on OperationId for metrics. They are preserved under all sampling modes, not only fixed-rate.

stem: A Coho Vineyard operations team creates a metric alert on CPU and expects one notification when the condition starts and one when it resolves, without a new fire on every evaluation. Which default behavior of metric alerts provides this?
choices: Metric alerts are stateless by default and fire each evaluation
Metric alerts are stateful by default, notifying on fire and on resolve
Metric alerts never send resolved notifications
Statefulness is available only for log search alerts
explanation: Metric alerts are stateful by default, so they notify once when fired and once when resolved rather than on every evaluation. Metric alerts are not stateless by default. They do send resolved notifications. Statefulness is configurable on log search alerts too, so it is not exclusive to them.

stem: Margie's Travel wants to be alerted when a virtual machine stops sending its heartbeat, that is, when log rows are absent. Microsoft guidance warns that log search alerts are weak at detecting a lack of data. Which alert approach is recommended for this absence-of-data scenario?
choices: A log search alert counting rows equal to zero
A metric alert, such as metric alerts for logs
explanation: Log data is latent and semi-structured, so detecting absence with log search alerts risks misfires; Microsoft recommends metric alerts, such as metric alerts for logs, for detecting a lack of data like a missing heartbeat. A row-count log alert is exactly the pattern the guidance cautions against for absence. Smart detection targets failure anomalies in web apps, not custom heartbeat absence. Activity log alerts track control-plane events, not VM heartbeat gaps.

stem: Blue Yonder Airlines enables dynamic thresholds on a brand-new metric alert and is surprised it does not fire immediately during an obvious spike. What minimum data condition must be met before dynamic thresholds trigger?
choices: At least 3 days and 30 samples of historical data
At least 10 samples in the last hour
explanation: Alert rules using dynamic thresholds do not trigger before collecting at least 3 days and 30 samples of data, so new resources wait until enough history exists. Weekly seasonality needs about three weeks, but that is not the minimum to fire. Ten samples in an hour is not the documented threshold. Some history is always required.

stem: A VanArsdel engineer wants a single metric alert rule that both uses dynamic thresholds and evaluates two separate conditions at once, but the portal will not allow it. Which limitation explains this?
choices: Dynamic thresholds cannot be used in alert rules that monitor multiple conditions
Multiple conditions require log search alerts only
Dynamic thresholds need purge protection enabled
explanation: You cannot use dynamic thresholds in alert rules that monitor multiple conditions; each dynamic-threshold rule evaluates a single condition. Dynamic thresholds are not tied to a 1-minute frequency (that restriction applies to log search alerts). Multiple static conditions are allowed on metric alerts. Purge protection is a Key Vault feature, unrelated to alerts.

stem: Trey Research wants an alert rule that, when it fires, sends an email to on-call, posts to a webhook, and triggers an Azure Function, with those actions reusable across many rules. Which Azure Monitor construct defines this reusable set of notifications and actions?
explanation: An action group is the reusable collection of notifications (email, SMS) and actions (webhook, Azure Function, Logic App) that alert rules invoke when they fire. Alert processing rules modify or suppress alerts rather than define the action set. Diagnostic settings route platform logs and metrics. Data collection rules govern log ingestion, not alert actions.

stem: Lucerne Publishing compares a metric alert with a log search alert for the same underlying signal and finds the metric alert reacts noticeably faster. Which characteristic best explains the difference?
choices: Log search alerts always run at 1-second frequency
Metric alerts offer near-real-time monitoring, while log data is inherently more latent
Log search alerts cannot be scheduled
explanation: Metric alerts provide near-real-time monitoring, whereas logs are semi-structured and more latent, so log search alerts react more slowly for the same underlying signal. Log search alerts do not run every second. Metric alerts still use evaluation windows. Log search alerts are scheduled at a chosen frequency, so scheduling is not the difference.

stem: Graphic Design Institute opens Application Map for a distributed app but sees two microservices collapsed into a single node. Which telemetry property determines how components are drawn as separate nodes on the map?
choices: The cloud role name (roleName or name)
explanation: Application Map identifies individual components by their roleName or name property; distinct role names render as separate nodes, so two services sharing a role name collapse into one. Operation_Id groups a single transaction, not component identity. The instrumentation key or connection string identifies the resource, not per-node roles. Session_Id tracks user sessions, not architecture nodes.

stem: A Humongous Insurance developer searches Transaction Search for HomeController.About by typing the fragment out and gets no results, yet searching about returns the item. Which search behavior explains this?
choices: Search matches complete words, not substrings
Search is case-sensitive on the operation name
explanation: Transaction Search matches complete words rather than substrings, so a fragment like out does not match, while the whole word about does. The mismatch is about word boundaries, not case. Search does look at property values including custom properties. It indexes many telemetry types, not only exceptions.

stem: The Phone Company is rolling out a hotfix and wants to watch request and failure counts update within about a second to validate the fix live, after which the data is not retained. Which Application Insights tool is purpose-built for this sub-second, non-retained view?
explanation: Live Metrics streams performance and failure counters with roughly one-second latency for real-time validation, and the stream is not retained. Application Map shows architecture and aggregated health, not a sub-second stream. Transaction Search inspects stored individual items. Profiler captures call-stack traces, not a live counter stream.

stem: Consolidated Messenger has a slow .NET operation and needs code-level call stacks with hot paths to find the bottleneck method, sampled from production traffic. Which Application Insights feature captures this?
explanation: Application Insights Profiler captures call stacks and hot paths for .NET operations from real traffic, exposing the methods that dominate response time. Live Metrics shows counters, not call stacks. Smart detection flags failure anomalies but does not produce call-stack traces. Availability tests probe endpoints from outside, not internal code paths.

stem: Best For You Organics needs a log search alert that evaluates each returned row individually for faster, near-real-time alerting at scale, rather than aggregating a count over a window. Which log alert option fits?
choices: A stateful aggregated log search alert
A metric alert with dynamic thresholds
explanation: Simple log search alerts evaluate each row individually for faster, near-real-time alerting at scale, unlike aggregated log search alerts. A stateful aggregated log alert computes an aggregation over the window rather than per row. A metric alert does not run a Log Analytics query per row. Smart detection is an automatic anomaly feature, not a per-row rule.

stem: A First Up Consultants analyst joins requests to dependencies in Log Analytics using join without specifying a kind, and notices duplicate left-side rows were collapsed. Which default join flavor produced this, and what does it do?
choices: inner, which keeps all matching pairs
leftouter, which keeps all left rows
innerunique, which deduplicates keys on the left side
fullouter, which keeps all rows from both tables
explanation: When kind is omitted, join uses innerunique, which removes duplicate keys from the left table before matching, a behavior tuned for log correlation scenarios. inner is the standard join but is not the default and does not dedupe the left. leftouter keeps unmatched left rows. fullouter keeps unmatched rows from both sides.

stem: A School of Fine Art report counts requests with summarize count() while SDK sampling is active, and the totals look too low. A reviewer says the query must account for sampling. Which change yields sampling-corrected counts?
choices: Multiply the result by the number of nodes
explanation: Each retained record carries an itemCount representing the items it stands in for, so summarize sum(itemCount) restores the true count when sampling is active. dcount(Id) counts distinct ids, not sampled volume. take limits rows and worsens accuracy. Node count is unrelated to the per-record itemCount weighting.

stem:
Complete the KQL so the request count is corrected for Application Insights sampling.

```
requests
| where timestamp > ago(1h)
| summarize corrected = ________(itemCount) by name
```
explanation: sum(itemCount) adds each retained record's itemCount weight, reconstructing the true request count under sampling. count() ignores itemCount and undercounts. avg(itemCount) gives a mean weight, not a total. dcount(itemCount) counts distinct weight values, which is meaningless here.

stem:
Complete the KQL that estimates the effective percentage of request telemetry retained under sampling.

```
requests
| summarize samplingPercent = 100 / ________(itemCount)
```
explanation: Each record represents on average itemCount items, so 100 divided by avg(itemCount) yields the effective retained sampling percentage. sum(itemCount) is the corrected total, not an average weight. count() is the raw retained row count. max(itemCount) uses a single extreme weight rather than the mean.

stem:
Complete the join so every request row is kept even when it has no matching dependency.

```
requests
| join kind=________ (
    dependencies
) on operation_Id
```
explanation: leftouter returns all rows from the left table (requests) plus matching dependency rows, preserving requests that have no dependency. inner and innerunique drop requests without a matching dependency. leftanti returns only requests with no match, discarding the matched ones.

stem:
Complete the join that returns only requests with no matching trace, to find operations missing their logs.

```
requests
| join kind=________ (
    traces
) on operation_Id
```
explanation: leftanti returns rows from the left table that have no match in the right table, exactly the requests missing a corresponding trace. leftouter keeps all left rows including matches. inner keeps only matches. fullouter keeps everything from both tables, not just the unmatched left rows.

stem:
Complete the KQL that builds a per-hour time series of request counts, filling empty bins with zero.

```
requests
| ________ total = count() default=0 on timestamp step 1h by name
```
explanation: make-series builds regularly spaced series along a time axis with a step and a default fill value for empty bins, producing arrays suitable for series analysis. summarize aggregates into rows without generating gap-filled series arrays. mv-expand expands arrays into rows. evaluate invokes plugins, not series construction.

stem:
Complete the KQL that groups average request duration into 5-minute time buckets.

```
requests
| summarize avg(duration) by ________(timestamp, 5m)
```
explanation: bin(timestamp, 5m) rounds each timestamp down to a 5-minute boundary, creating the time buckets that summarize groups by. floor rounds numbers but is not the time-bucket idiom here. startofday truncates to a day, not 5 minutes. range generates a series of values, not a grouping expression.

stem:
Complete the KQL that returns the 95th percentile of request duration per operation.

```
requests
| summarize p95 = ________(duration, 95) by name
```
explanation: percentile(duration, 95) estimates the nearest-rank 95th percentile of the column within each group. avg returns the mean, not a percentile. max returns the single highest value. percentiles takes one or more percentile arguments and returns multiple columns, so it does not fit this single-value syntax.

stem:
Complete the KQL that returns only the five operations with the highest average duration.

```
requests
| summarize avgDur = avg(duration) by name
| ________ 5 by avgDur desc
```
explanation: top 5 by avgDur desc sorts by average duration and returns the five highest rows in one operator. take and its alias limit return an arbitrary unordered five rows. sample returns a random subset. Neither take nor limit sorts before truncating.

stem: A Wide World Importers team enables the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Distro on an ASP.NET Core app for production. Which two actions correctly establish where telemetry is sent and the component identity? (Select two.)
choices: Set APPLICATIONINSIGHTS_CONNECTION_STRING to the resource connection string
Set OTEL_SERVICE_NAME to the component's role name
Set an instrumentation key as a URL query parameter
Enable the Key Vault admin account
explanation: The connection string (via environment variable) tells the Distro which Application Insights resource to send to, and OTEL_SERVICE_NAME sets the service.name resource attribute used as the Cloud Role Name. Instrumentation keys are deprecated in favor of connection strings and never belong in a URL. OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER=None disables trace export entirely. The Key Vault admin account is unrelated to telemetry configuration.

stem: A Southridge Video team is choosing between metric alerts and log search alerts. Which two statements are accurate for their design? (Select two.)
choices: Metric alerts provide near-real-time evaluation and are stateful by default
Log search alerts can run arbitrary Log Analytics (KQL) queries at a set frequency
Log search alerts are the recommended choice for detecting absence of data
Metric alerts require a KQL query for every condition
Metric alerts cannot send a resolved notification
explanation: Metric alerts evaluate metrics in near real time and are stateful by default; log search alerts run KQL queries against logs at a chosen frequency for advanced logic. For absence of data, metric alerts are recommended over log alerts. Metric alerts evaluate metrics directly and do not need a KQL query per condition. Metric alerts do send resolved notifications.

stem: A Nod Publishers engineer reviews how adaptive sampling behaves in the classic Application Insights SDKs. Which two statements are correct? (Select two.)
choices: Adaptive sampling is enabled by default in the ASP.NET and ASP.NET Core SDKs
Adaptive sampling adjusts the sampling percentage automatically as telemetry volume changes
Adaptive sampling is the default sampling mode in the Java agent
Adaptive sampling synchronizes browser and server sampling decisions
Adaptive sampling requires you to set a fixed sampling percentage manually
explanation: Adaptive sampling is on by default in the ASP.NET and ASP.NET Core SDKs and automatically raises or lowers the sampling percentage based on observed telemetry volume. Java does not support adaptive sampling. Synchronizing client and server decisions is a property of fixed-rate sampling. Adaptive sampling sets the rate automatically rather than requiring a manual fixed percentage.

stem: An Alpine Ski House team plans to use dynamic thresholds on Azure Monitor alerts. Which two constraints must they account for? (Select two.)
choices: Dynamic thresholds cannot be used in rules that monitor multiple conditions
Dynamic thresholds cannot be used in log search alert rules with 1-minute frequency
Dynamic thresholds require purge protection on the workspace
Dynamic thresholds work only with fixed static bounds you supply
Dynamic thresholds ignore historical data entirely
explanation: Dynamic thresholds cannot be applied to multi-condition rules, and they cannot be used in log search alert rules that run at 1-minute frequency. Purge protection is a Key Vault feature, not a dynamic-threshold prerequisite. Dynamic thresholds compute bounds from history rather than requiring static bounds, and they rely on about 10 days of historical data rather than ignoring it.
